Explanation
A combination of glutamate dehydrogenase and toxin assay can be used for the detection of Clostridium difficile. 
Clostridium difficile is a gram-positive anaerobic bacillus that causes Clostridioides (formerly Clostridium) difficile infection after ingestion of spores of the organism. The more severe form of the condition is known as pseudomembranous colitis (PMC). Enzyme immunoassay to detect glutamate dehydrogenase is less specific compared to toxin detection for diagnosis. So a combination of the two can be used for diagnostic confirmation.
The condition is most commonly associated with prolonged antimicrobial use, which interferes with the commensal colonic microflora. The most commonly implicated antibiotics are cephalosporins, ampicillin, and clindamycin. The spores are spread by contact with the feces of affected individuals or asymptomatic carriers. It can persist on surfaces for months. Risk factors include poor hand hygiene, old age, and gastrointestinal surgery.
The spores germinate in the small intestine and produce two toxins—toxin A (enterotoxin) and toxin B (cytotoxin). These interfere with the epithelial-cell barrier function and result in diarrhea and pseudomembrane formation. The pseudomembranes appear as small whitish-yellow plaques initially which later coalesce to involve the entire colon wall. It contains necrotic leukocytes, fibrin, and cellular debris. The anamnestic IgG response determines which patients develop the disease or remain asymptomatic. 
Symptoms include diarrhea, fever, and abdominal pain. The diagnosis is based on a combination of clinical criteria and detection of toxin or the organism in stool samples. This can be done by nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) methods such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or by culture. 
Discontinuation of any ongoing antimicrobials and adequate hydration are general measures that are recommended. Oral fidaxomicin or vancomycin is the first-line treatment. Oral metronidazole can be used when these are not available.
Other options:
Option A: Aerobic culture of stool is the most sensitive test and is highly specific. It is not used practically as the turnaround time is slow.

Enveloped DNA viruses (HHP): {{c1::Hepadna (HBV), Herpes (HHV), Pox}}. Non-enveloped DNA (PPAP): {{c2::Papilloma, Polyoma, Adeno, Parvo}}. Non-enveloped RNA (PC-HAR): {{c3::Picorna, Calici, Hepe, Astro, Reo}}. Paradox NA: {{c4::ssDNA = Parvo; dsRNA = Rota}}.
answer: Size: Biggest virus = Poxvirus; Smallest virus = Parvovirus.

question: Viral genomes & shapes: {{c1::HIV}} (2 RNA copies), {{c2::Influenza}} (8 segments), {{c3::Rotavirus}} (11 segments), {{c4::HBV}} (partially ds circular), {{c5::HPV}} (completely ds circular). Shapes: Pox = {{c6::Box}}, Rabies = {{c7::Bullet}}, Ebola = {{c8::Filamentous}}.
answer: Inclusion bodies: Intranuclear = HSV (Cowdry A), CMV (Owl eye), YFV (Torres/Councilman); Intracytoplasmic = Rabies (Negri).

question: Cytopathic effects: Measles = {{c1::Syncytium}}; Adenovirus = {{c2::Granular clumping / bunch of grapes}}; HSV = {{c3::Ballooning}}; Enterovirus = {{c4::Crenation}}. Viral quantification: {{c5::Pock assay}} (CAM of egg) vs {{c6::Plaque assay}} (tissue culture, M/C).
answer: Dengue timing: <5 days symptoms → detect virus (PCR/NS1 Ag); ≥5 days → detect Ab.

question: Protozoa locomotory organs: Cilia = {{c1::Balantidium coli}}; Pseudopodia = {{c2::Entamoeba histolytica}} & free-living amoebae ({{c3::Naegleria, Acanthamoeba, Balamuthia, Sappinia}}); Flagella = {{c4::Giardia, Leishmania, Trypanosoma, Trichomonas}}; None = {{c5::Sporozoa/Coccidia}}.

Non-bile stained eggs (NEHA): {{c1::Necator, Enterobius, H. nana, Ancylostoma}}. Autoinfective helminths: {{c2::T. solium, H. nana, Enterobius, Strongyloides}}. Cancers: {{c3::S. haematobium}} (Bladder Ca), {{c4::S. japonicum}} (Colon Ca), {{c5::Clonorchis/Opisthorchis}} (Cholangiocarcinoma).

Hand hygiene: {{c1::Handwash (soap & water, 40–60 sec)}} for visibly soiled hands > {{c2::Handrub (20–30 sec)}}. PPE Donning: {{c3::Hand hygiene → Gown → Mask → Goggles/Face shield → Gloves}}. Doffing: {{c4::Gloves → Gown → Goggles/Face shield → Mask → Hand hygiene}}.
answer: WHO 5 moments: Before & after patient, before & after procedures/fluid exposure, after patient surroundings.

question: BMW Bags: {{c1::Yellow}} (soiled cotton, tissues, medicines, blood bags → Incineration); {{c2::Red}} (plastic urine bags, rubber gloves → Autoclave + Recycling); {{c3::White}} (metallic sharps/needles → NaOCl + shredding/encapsulation); {{c4::Blue}} (glass/metals → NaOCl + recycling).
answer: Mercury spill: Aspirate in syringe → store in container with water → handover to BMW collectors.

question: Sterilization biological controls: {{c1::Autoclave (121°C, 15 min, 15 psi)}} & {{c2::H2O2 Plasma}} = Bacillus stearothermophilus; {{c3::Hot air oven (160°C, 2 hr)}} & {{c4::ETO}} = Bacillus subtilis / atrophaeus; {{c5::Ionising radiation}} = Bacillus pumilus.
answer: Media exceptions: Loeffler's serum slope & LJ medium are sterilized by Inspissation (not Autoclave).

question: Spaulding's classification: {{c1::Critical}} (sterile site, surgical instruments) → Sterilisation > HLD; {{c2::Semi-critical}} (mucous membrane, flexible endoscopes) → {{c3::HLD (Glutaraldehyde > OPA)}}; {{c4::Non-critical}} (intact skin, stethoscope) → ILD/LLD. Blood spill: {{c5::1% Na hypochlorite}}.
answer: Disinfectant tests: Chick-Martin (with organic matter), Rideal-Walker (without organic matter), Kelsey-Sykes (capacity), Maurer's (in-use).

question: Innate immunity: {{c1::immediate (3–4 hrs)}}, recognizes genetic patterns via {{c2::PRR}}, non-specific, no memory. Acquired immunity: {{c3::5–7 days}}, antigens via {{c4::APC}}, T-cells (CMI) & B-cells (Humoral), specific with memory. MHC gene is on {{c5::Chromosome 6p}}.
answer: Passive acquired immunity: Maternal IgG, PEP IgG, blood transfusion IgG.

question: T-cell activation needs 3 signals: Ag presentation ({{c1::MHC-I/II to TCR}}), Co-stimulatory ({{c2::B7 to CD28}}), and Cytokine ({{c3::IL-1/IL-2}}). {{c4::Superantigens}} (TSST, S. aureus enterotoxin) bind to the {{c5::lateral side of β-chain}} of MHC-II & TCR.
answer: Th1 vs Th2: IL-12 → Th1 → IFN-γ (CMI); IL-4,5 → Th2 → B-cells → Ab (HI).

question: Antibody classes: {{c1::IgM}} (pentamer, highest MW, 1st formed); {{c2::IgG}} (monomer, crosses placenta, highest serum concentration, IgG2 against capsulated bugs); {{c3::Secretory IgA}} (dimer, mucosal immunity); {{c4::IgD}} (B-cell receptor); {{c5::IgE}} (Type 1 hypersensitivity & parasites).
answer: Germinal centre of LN: Somatic hypermutation, affinity maturation, class switching.

question: Hypersensitivity: {{c1::Type 1}} (IgE, anaphylaxis, ABPA), {{c2::Type 2}} (cytotoxic, AIHA, Goodpasture), {{c3::Type 3}} (immune complex, Arthus, serum sickness, Type 2 lepra reaction), {{c4::Type 4}} (delayed CMI, Mantoux, Type 1 lepra reaction). {{c5::GVHD}} occurs in bone marrow/thymus allografts.
answer: Graft rejection: Hyperacute (hours, Type 2 HI); Acute/Chronic (Type 4 CMI).

question: IDD: {{c1::Bruton's}} (X-linked, BTK, no B-cells/Ig), {{c2::DiGeorge}} (22q11, 3rd/4th pouch, CATCH), {{c3::CGD}} (X-linked, Phox/NADPH oxidase, NBT +ve, S. aureus), {{c4::Chediak-Higashi}} (AR, LYST, giant granules, albinism). Complement: {{c5::C5b-C9 (MAC)}} deficiency → disseminated Neisseria.
answer: Other CDD: C1/C4/C2 → SLE; C1 esterase → HAE; DAF → PNH.

question: Meningeal signs: {{c1::Brudzinski's sign}} = involuntary flexion of hips & knees on neck flexion; {{c2::Kernig's sign}} = resistance to knee extension when hip is flexed.
answer: ABM M/C: Adults = Pneumococcus; Children = H. influenzae b; Neonates = GBS (world), E. coli (India), Listeria.

question: Identify the meningeal irritation sign shown: {{c1::Kernig's sign}} (resistance/pain on knee extension with hip flexed).
answer: CBM: M. tuberculosis causes cobweb coagulum with markedly elevated CSF protein.

question: Adult ABM: {{c1::Pneumococcus}} (GPC pairs, optochin sensitive), {{c2::Meningococcus}} (intracellular GNC pairs, Thayer-Martin, maltose fermenter), {{c3::H. influenzae b}} (satellitism around S. aureus on blood agar). Neonatal {{c4::Listeria}} shows {{c5::tumbling motility at 22°C}} (non-motile at 37°C).
answer: Rx: Adults = Vancomycin + Ceftriaxone; Neonates = Ampicillin + Ceftriaxone.

question: Viral encephalitis: {{c1::HSV-1}} (M/C sporadic temporal lobe, Rx Acyclovir), {{c2::JC virus}} (PML white brain disease), {{c3::JE}} (M/C overall, Culex, SA-14-14-2 live vaccine), {{c4::Nipah}} (fruit bat), {{c5::Rabies}} (Saliva PCR > CSF; DFA skin nape of neck), {{c6::Measles SSPE}} (7–10 yrs later).
answer: Rabies PEP: Wash with soap & water → antiseptics → Ig → killed vaccine in deltoid.

question: Free-living amoebic encephalitis: {{c1::Naegleria fowleri}} (acute PAM, lobe-like pseudopodia, Rx Liposomal Amphotericin B), {{c2::Sappinia}} (bilobed nucleus), {{c3::Acanthamoeba}} (chronic GAE & contact lens keratitis, thorn-like pseudopodia), {{c4::Balamuthia}} (branching pseudopodia).

Poliovirus (stool PCR): 99% asymptomatic, 1% meningitis, {{c1::0.1% acute flaccid paralysis}} (1:1000 iceberg). {{c2::OPV (Sabin, live)}} complications: VDPV (Type 2) & VAPP (Type 3). {{c3::fIPV (Salk, killed)}} given at 6, 14 weeks & 9 months.

{{c1::Clostridium botulinum}} (botulinum toxin) blocks {{c2::Acetylcholine}} → {{c3::flaccid paralysis}}; {{c4::Clostridium tetani}} (tetanospasmin) blocks {{c5::Glycine & GABA}} → {{c6::spastic paralysis}}. Both grow on RCM; toxin detected by ELISA; Rx Antitoxin + Metronidazole/Penicillin.
answer: Tetanus PEP: Clean wound ≥3 doses needs Td if ≥10 yrs; Dirty wound ≥3 doses needs Td if ≥5 yrs; <3/unknown dirty wound needs Td + Ig.

question: Infective Endocarditis: Vascular = {{c1::Janeway lesions}} (painless bleeding spots on palms/soles); Immunological = {{c2::Osler's nodes}} (painful nodules) & {{c3::Roth's spots}} (retinal hemorrhages). Etiology: Native = {{c4::S. aureus}}; Early prosthetic (<1 yr) = {{c5::S. epidermidis}}; Late (>1 yr) = {{c6::S. viridans}}.
answer: Modified Duke's: 2 major, OR 1 major + 3 minor, OR 5 minor.

question: Acute Rheumatic Fever (non-suppurative GAS complication) Major Jones criteria: {{c1::Pancarditis, Arthritis (migratory polyarthritis; mono in high-risk), Sydenham's chorea, Subcutaneous nodules, Erythema marginatum}}. Rx: {{c2::Penicillin}} (Erythromycin if allergic).
answer: Diagnosis: 2 major OR 1 major + 2 minor OR 3 minor + past h/o ARF.

question: HIV structural genes: {{c1::env}} (gp120, gp41), {{c2::gag}} (p24), {{c3::pol}} (RT, protease, integrase). Stage 3: {{c4::Oral candidiasis}} (scraped off) vs {{c5::Oral hairy leukoplakia (EBV)}} (not removed), Pulmonary TB. Stage 4 (AIDS): {{c6::Kaposi's sarcoma (M/C cancer)}}.
answer: Rx: TLD (Tenofovir + Lamivudine + Dolutegravir) lifelong; PEP = TLD × 28 days.

question: HIV CD4 opportunistic infections: <500 = {{c1::TB, Candida, VZV}}; <200 = {{c2::Cryptosporidium, Pneumocystis}}; <100 = {{c3::Toxoplasma, Histoplasma}}; <50 = {{c4::MAC, Cryptococcus, CMV}}. Congenital HIV: {{c5::Dried blood spot PCR}} at 6 wks, 6 mo, 12 mo → Ab at 18 mo.
answer: Window period (3 wks–3 mo): PCR > p24 Ag. NACO: 2 +ve if symptomatic, 3 +ve if asymptomatic.

question: VHF: {{c1::KFD}} (Ixodid tick, monkey amplifier, Karnataka), {{c2::Dengue}} (Aedes aegypti, re-infection ADE → DHF/DSS), {{c3::Yellow fever}} (absent in India, 17-D live vaccine), {{c4::CCHF}} (Ixodid tick, Gujarat), {{c5::Ebola/Marburg}} (fruit bat, septic shock).
answer: Dengue Ix: <5 days = PCR/NS1 Ag; ≥5 days = Ab detection.

question: Leishmaniasis (Vector: {{c1::Sandfly / Phlebotomus}}; Bihar endemic): {{c2::L. tropica}} (Oriental sore), {{c3::L. braziliensis}} (Espundia), {{c4::L. donovani}} (Kala-azar → PKDL). PBS shows {{c5::amastigote LD bodies with kinetoplast}} inside macrophages. DOC: {{c6::Liposomal Amphotericin B / Miltefosine}}.
answer: Rapid test: Detects Ab against rK39 Ag.

question: {{c1::American (Chagas)}}: T. cruzi, vector {{c2::Reduviid bug}}, mega-esophagus/heart/colon, {{c3::Romana's sign}}, Rx Benznidazole. {{c4::African (Sleeping sickness)}}: T. brucei, vector {{c5::Tse-tse fly}}, {{c6::Winterbottom sign}}, Rx Suramin. PBS shows {{c7::trypomastigote}}.
answer: Morphology: Spindle-shaped trypomastigote with folded undulating membrane/flagella.

question: Malaria PBS: {{c1::P. vivax}} (pLDH, single ring, schizont seen, round gametocyte, {{c2::Schuffner's dots}}) vs {{c3::P. falciparum}} (pLDH + HRP-2, {{c4::multiple rings}}, no schizont in PBS, {{c5::banana/sickle gametocyte}}, {{c6::Maurer's clefts}}).
answer: Complications: Cerebral malaria, Blackwater fever, ATN (P. falciparum); Nephrotic syndrome (P. malariae). Rx: P. vivax = CQ + Primaquine; P. falciparum = ACT.

question: {{c1::Babesia}} (Ixodid tick) shows {{c2::Maltese cross merozoites}} in RBCs (Rx Atovaquone ± Azithromycin). {{c3::Toxoplasma}} (cat oocysts) congenital triad: {{c4::Chorioretinitis, Hydrocephalus, Diffuse brain calcifications}}; acute vs chronic by {{c5::IgG avidity}} (Rx Pyrimethamine+Sulfadiazine; Pregnancy: {{c6::Spiramycin}}).
answer: Toxoplasma smear: Spindle-shaped tachyzoites; Sabin-Feldman dye test detects IgG.

question: Schistosomiasis (blood fluke, Rx {{c1::Praziquantel}}): {{c2::S. haematobium}} (urine, {{c3::terminal spine}}, bladder cancer), {{c4::S. mansoni}} (stool, {{c5::lateral spine}}), {{c6::S. japonicum}} (stool, {{c7::lateral knob}}, colorectal cancer).
answer: Also known as: Katayama fever / Swimmer's itch.

question: Filariasis (Culex vector): Lymphatic = {{c1::W. bancrofti}} (sheath +, no tail nuclei) & {{c2::B. malayi}} (sheath +, 2 tail nuclei), Rx DEC; Subcutaneous = {{c3::Loa loa}} (Calabar swelling, multiple tail nuclei) & {{c4::Onchocerca volvulus}} (River blindness, sheath -, Rx {{c5::Ivermectin}}).
answer: DEC provocation test: Give DEC tablet → larvae enter bloodstream in 30–60 min for daytime PBS.

question: {{c1::C. diphtheriae}}: pseudomembrane, bull neck, Albert stain ({{c2::metachromatic/Babes-Ernst granules, Chinese letter}}), potassium tellurite BA, Elek's test. {{c3::B. pertussis}}: whooping cough, {{c4::thumbprint appearance}}, Bordet-Gengou medium, Rx Azithromycin. {{c5::M. tb}}: new 4-mo regimen {{c6::2HPZM + 2HPM}}.
answer: TB latent tests: Mantoux & IGRA; Resistance = CBNAAT (rpoB).

question: Typical pneumonia M/C causes: Community = {{c1::Pneumococcus}}; Hospital = {{c2::S. aureus}}; Cystic fibrosis = {{c3::Pseudomonas}}; VAP = {{c4::Acinetobacter}}; Zoonotic horse = {{c5::Burkholderia mallei}}; Cattle = {{c6::Bacillus anthracis}} (medusa head/bamboo stick).
answer: Burkholderia: B. pseudomallei (Melioidosis), B. cepacia (Cepacia syndrome from contaminated IVF).

question: Bacterial atypical pneumonia (Rx {{c1::Azithromycin > Levofloxacin}}): {{c2::Chlamydia}} (McCoy/HeLa cell culture), {{c3::Mycoplasma}} (M/C overall, PPLO agar {{c4::fried-egg colonies}}, no Gram stain), {{c5::Legionella}} (whirlpools/humidifiers, {{c6::BCYE agar}}, urine Ag).

Viral pneumonia: {{c1::Influenza}} (8 segments, HA/NA; pandemic = {{c2::Ag shift}}, epidemic = {{c3::Ag drift}}; Rx Oseltamivir), {{c4::Corona}} (spike/flower petal), {{c5::Adeno}} (satellite/spacecraft). Parasitic lung fluke: {{c6::Paragonimus westermani}} (operculated egg in stool & sputum, Rx Praziquantel).
answer: Paragonimus egg: Thickened abopercular end.

question: Dimorphic fungi: {{c1::Histoplasma}} (intracellular in macrophage, tuberculate conidia), {{c2::Blastomyces}} (broad-based budding), {{c3::Coccidioides}} (spherule with endospores), {{c4::Paracoccidioides}} (Mickey Mouse/pilot wheel), {{c5::Talaromyces marneffei}} (oval yeast with septum, bottle-brush, red pigment on SDA).
answer: Rx: IV Liposomal Amphotericin B / Oral Itraconazole.

question: {{c1::Candida}} (yeast-like, pseudohyphae, {{c2::Germ tube / Reynolds-Braude +ve}} in C. albicans & C. dubliniensis, CHROMagar) vs {{c3::Cryptococcus}} (yeast, India ink halo, {{c4::Bird seed agar}} brown melanin colonies; Rx Liposomal Amp-B + Flucytosine × 2 wks → Fluconazole × 8 wks).

{{c1::Aspergillus}} (neutropenia, β-DG & galactomannan, narrow {{c2::acute-angle dichotomous hyphae}}, Rx {{c3::Voriconazole}}) vs {{c4::Mucorales}} (DKA/iron/post-COVID, rhinocerebral black lesions, broad {{c5::obtuse/right-angle ribbon hyphae}}, Rx Surgery + Lipo-Amp-B/Posaconazole).
answer: LPCB vesicles: 1/3rd = A. fumigatus; 2/3rd = A. flavus; Complete = A. niger. Rhizoids: Nodal = Rhizopus; Internodal = Absidia; None = Mucor.

question: {{c1::Pneumocystis jirovecii}} (atypical fungus, CD4 < 200): BAL > sputum; {{c2::GMS stain}} shows {{c3::crushed ping-pong ball / black cysts}}; β-DG +ve; Rx {{c4::Cotrimoxazole}}.

{{c1::Helicobacter pylori}} (peptic ulcer → gastric Ca): Gram-negative comma-shaped, corkscrew motility, {{c2::Urease +ve}} (differentiates from Campylobacter), Skirrow's media. Triple therapy (Clarithromycin + Metronidazole/Amoxicillin + Omeprazole) or Quadruple (+ Bismuth) × 2 weeks.
answer: Non-invasive tests: Urea breath test & stool Ag.

question: Pre-formed toxins (<6h): {{c1::S. aureus}} (milk, enterotoxin), {{c2::Bacillus cereus}} (fried rice, emetic toxin); >16h: {{c3::C. botulinum}} (canned food). Post-formed (>6h): {{c4::Vibrio cholerae}} (rice-watery), {{c5::EHEC O157:H7}} & {{c6::Shigella}} (dysentery & HUS).
answer: Salmonella carriers: Screening = Vi antibody; Confirmatory = Urine/stool culture.

question: {{c1::Vibrio cholerae}} (darting motility/fish-in-stream, {{c2::yellow colonies}} on TCBS, String +ve, Cholera red +ve) vs {{c3::V. parahaemolyticus}} ({{c4::green colonies}} on TCBS, {{c5::Kanagawa phenomenon}} on Wagatsuma agar, String -ve). Rx: {{c6::Doxycycline}}.
answer: Campylobacter: S-shaped, Skirrow's media, Urease -ve. Salmonella: Wilson-Blair media, Widal +ve.

question: Viral GE: {{c1::Rotavirus}} (M/C in <2 yrs, {{c2::11-segment dsRNA}}, stool Ag ELISA, live oral vaccine), {{c3::Norovirus}} (M/C in adults), Adenovirus 40/41, Astrovirus.

Non-acid-fast protozoal GE: {{c1::Balantidium coli}} (cilia, round cyst 2 nuclei, Rx Tetracycline), {{c2::Entamoeba histolytica}} (pseudopodia/RBCs, flask-shaped ulcer, round cyst 4 nuclei, Rx Metronidazole + Diloxanide), {{c3::Giardia lamblia}} (falling-leaf motility, 2 suckers, 8 flagella, oval cyst 4 nuclei).

Acid-fast protozoal GE: {{c1::Cryptosporidium}} (round 4–5 μm, autoinfection, Rx {{c2::Nitazoxanide}}), {{c3::Cyclospora}} (round 8–10 μm, Rx Cotrimoxazole), {{c4::Cystoisospora}} (oval 15–30 μm, Rx Cotrimoxazole).
answer: Key size rule: Crypto (4–5) < Cyclo (8–10) < Cysto (15–30).

question: Cestode eggs (Rx Praziquantel): {{c1::Taenia solium}} (non-acid-fast embryophore; causes neurocysticercosis → Rx Steroids + Albendazole), {{c2::T. saginata}} (acid-fast), {{c3::H. nana}} (polar filaments), {{c4::D. latum}} (operculum + knob; megaloblastic anemia).
answer: Fasciola buski: Intestinal fluke with large operculated egg.

question: GI Nematodes: {{c1::Strongyloides}} (parthenogenic, larva in stool, hyperinfection, Rx Ivermectin), {{c2::Hookworm}} (segmented blastomeres, IDA), {{c3::Ascaris}} (mammillated/semilunar chitin sheath, intestinal obstruction), {{c4::Enterobius}} (D-shaped planoconvex egg, perianal itching), {{c5::Trichuris}} (barrel-shaped with bipolar mucus plugs, rectal prolapse).
answer: Loeffler's pulmonary eosinophilia: Seen with Strongyloides, Hookworm, Ascaris.

question: Viral Hepatitis: {{c1::HAV & HEV}} (feco-oral, IgM ELISA, HEV high mortality in pregnancy); {{c2::HBV}} (HBsAg, Anti-HBc IgM acute vs IgG chronic, HBeAg infectivity, Rx Tenofovir, subunit vaccine); {{c3::HCV}} (PCR confirmatory, Sofosbuvir + Velpatasvir); {{c4::HDV}} (coinfection IgM HBV vs superinfection IgG HBV).

Hydatid cyst ({{c1::Echinococcus granulosus}}, dog tapeworm): Liver (M/c) > lung; USG/CT shows {{c2::Water lily sign}}; confirmatory Antibody ELISA; Rx {{c3::PAIR}} (Puncture-Aspiration-Injection-Reaspiration) + {{c4::Albendazole}}.

Genital ulcers: {{c1::Donovanosis}} (K. granulomatis, painless, pseudobuboes, Donovan bodies in macrophage, Azithromycin); {{c2::Chancroid}} (H. ducreyi, painful ulcer & bubos, Azithromycin); {{c3::Syphilis}} (T. pallidum, painless, dark-field spirochetes, Penicillin); {{c4::LGV}} (C. trachomatis, painless ulcer + painful bubos).
answer: Key: Only Chancroid has BOTH painful ulcer & painful bubo.

question: Vaginitis: {{c1::Trichomonas vaginalis}} (yellow-green fishy discharge, 5 flagella, jerky motility, Metronidazole); {{c2::Gardnerella vaginalis}} (white fishy discharge, {{c3::Clue cells}}, Metronidazole); {{c4::Candida albicans}} (curdy-white discharge, severe itching, pseudohyphae, Fluconazole).
answer: Gardnerella: Vaginal epithelial cells coated with coccobacilli.

question: {{c1::Gonococcal urethritis}} (<1 wk, purulent discharge, {{c2::kidney-shaped GNC in pairs inside neutrophils}}, Thayer-Martin, non-maltose fermenter, Rx {{c3::Ceftriaxone}}) vs {{c4::Non-gonococcal urethritis}} (>1 wk, M/C = Chlamydia trachomatis).
answer: Differentiation from Meningococcus: Gonococcus does NOT ferment maltose.

question: {{c1::S. aureus}} (clusters, β-hemolysis large colonies, Coagulase +ve; MSSA Penicillin, MRSA Vancomycin, VRSA Daptomycin/Linezolid) vs {{c2::S. pyogenes}} (chains, β-hemolysis pin-point, {{c3::Bacitracin sensitive}}) vs {{c4::S. agalactiae}} ({{c5::CAMP test +ve}}).
answer: S. aureus M/C: Abscess, burn wound, native IE, HAP, osteomyelitis.

question: {{c1::Bacillus anthracis}} (hide porter's malignant pustule/black eschar, wool sorter's pneumonia, {{c2::bamboo stick}} non-bulging spores, medusa head/string of pearls, Ciprofloxacin) vs {{c3::Clostridium perfringens}} (gas gangrene alpha toxin, {{c4::club-shaped}} subterminal bulging spores, Nagler +ve).

{{c1::Actinomyces}} (anaerobic, lumpy jaw with dark-yellow sulphur granules, {{c2::sunray appearance}}, {{c3::non-acid-fast}}, Rx Penicillin) vs {{c4::Nocardia}} (aerobic, Madura foot, filamentous GPB, {{c5::acid-fast}}, Rx {{c6::Welsh regimen: Amikacin + Cotrimoxazole}}).

{{c1::Mycobacterium leprae}} (non-cultivable, slit skin smear, {{c2::cigar bundle}} acid-fast, mice/armadillo; Rx Rifampicin + Dapsone + Clofazimine). Paucibacillary (≤5 patches, 0 nerves) vs Multibacillary (>5 patches, ≥1 nerve). {{c3::Type 1 lepra}} = Type 4 HSR; {{c4::Type 2 (ENL)}} = Type 3 HSR.
answer: Lepra reaction Rx: Continue MDT + start steroids.

question: HHV-1/2/3 vesicles show {{c1::multinucleated Tzanck giant cells}}. {{c2::HHV-4 (EBV)}} (IMN, Burkitt's, NPC), {{c3::HHV-5 (CMV)}} (post-transplant <3 mo), {{c4::BK virus}} (post-transplant nephropathy >3 mo), {{c5::HHV-8}} (Kaposi sarcoma).

{{c1::Molluscum contagiosum}} (umbilicated papules, no vaccine). {{c2::HPV}} low-risk {{c3::6, 11}} (warts) vs high-risk {{c4::16, 18}} (E6 inhibits p53, E7 inhibits Rb; Gardasil-9). {{c5::Parvovirus B19}}: children = slapped cheek; sickle cell = {{c6::aplastic crisis}}; congenital = hydrops.
answer: RNA exanthems: Measles (Koplik spots, Edmonston-Zagreb), Rubella (Forchheimer spots, RA 27/3), Coxsackie A16/EV71 (HFMD).

question: {{c1::Malassezia globosa}} (M/C) > furfur causes {{c2::Tinea/Pityriasis versicolor}} (hypo/hyperpigmented patches on upper trunk). Wood's lamp = {{c3::golden yellow fluorescence}}; KOH mount = {{c4::spaghetti & meatball appearance}}; Urease +ve.
answer: Rx: Topical Ketoconazole/Clotrimazole; Oral Itraconazole/Fluconazole.

question: Tinea capitis (Wood's lamp = {{c1::apple green}}): {{c2::Kerion}} (boggy, T. verrucosum), {{c3::Favus}} (scutula crusts, T. schoenleinii), {{c4::Ectothrix}} (M. canis), {{c5::Endothrix}} (black dots, T. tonsurans). Macroconidia: {{c6::Trichophyton}} (pencil), {{c7::Microsporum}} (boat), {{c8::Epidermophyton}} (club).
answer: Rx: Scalp = Oral Griseofulvin; Other sites = Itraconazole/Fluconazole. Hair perforation +ve = T. mentagrophytes.

question: {{c1::Eumycetoma}} (Madurella mycetomatis, black granules), {{c2::Sporotrichosis}} (Sporothrix schenckii, lymphocutaneous nodules, {{c3::asteroid body}} & flower-like conidia), {{c4::Chromoblastomycosis}} (verrucous lesions, {{c5::Medlar / copper penny bodies}}).
answer: Phaeohyphomycosis (Bipolaris): Medlar bodies absent. Rx: Oral Itraconazole / IV Lipo-Amp-B.

question: Viviparous skin/MSK nematodes: {{c1::Trichinella spiralis}} (man/pig, myalgia & myocarditis, muscle biopsy {{c2::spiral larva}}, Bachman test +ve, Rx Albendazole) and {{c3::Dracunculus medinensis}} (man/cyclops, adult worm from {{c4::ruptured skin blister}}, Rx worm removal).
answer: Filarial worm: Also viviparous (lymphatic & subcutaneous tissue).

question: Bacterial toxin MOA: {{c1::↑cAMP}} (Anthrax toxin, Cholera toxin via GM1); {{c2::- Rho-GTPase}} (C. difficile A & B); {{c3::- EF-2}} (Diphtheria toxin, Pseudomonas Exotoxin A); {{c4::- Ribosomes}} (EHEC verocytotoxin, Shiga toxin).
answer: C. difficile trigger: Prolonged Ceftriaxone/Ampicillin/Clindamycin; Rx Fidaxomicin.

question: Vector diseases (DOC {{c1::Doxycycline}}; Plague = {{c2::Streptomycin > Doxycycline}}): {{c3::Rat flea}} (Plague, Endemic typhus), {{c4::Louse}} (Epidemic typhus, Epidemic relapsing fever, Trench fever), {{c5::Hard tick}} (Lyme's target rash, RMSF), {{c6::Soft tick}} (Endemic relapsing fever, Q fever), {{c7::Mite}} (Scrub typhus black eschar, Rickettsial pox).
answer: Leptospirosis (Rat): Calf tenderness + conjunctival suffusion + hepatosplenomegaly.

question: Congenital TORCH: {{c1::CMV}} (M/C overall, periventricular calcifications), {{c2::Rubella}} (M/C in 1st trimester; cataract, SNHL, PDA), {{c3::Toxoplasma}} (diffuse calcifications, chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus), {{c4::Syphilis}} (keratitis, SNHL, Hutchinson teeth), {{c5::Zika}} (microcephaly), {{c6::VZV}} (cicatrization, limb hypoplasia).

{{c1::Prion (CJD)}}: misfolding of PrPC → PrPSc → amyloid plaques & spongiform encephalopathy; EEG = {{c2::triphasic high-voltage discharges}}; MRI = {{c3::cortical ribboning}}; confirmatory CSF ELISA. Bioterrorism Cat A: {{c4::Anthrax, Botulism, Plague (BSL-3)}} and {{c5::Smallpox, Ebola, Marburg (BSL-4)}}.
answer: BSL-2: Gastroenteritis bacteria (Cat B); BSL-3: Nipah, H1N1, Corona, M.tb (Cat C).

question: Who is known as the Father of Microbiology, developed liquid culture media, autoclave, pasteurization, and CAR vaccines (Cholera, Anthrax, Rabies)? {{c1::Louis Pasteur}}
answer: Also: Disproved abiogenesis & proposed germ theory of disease.

question: Who is the Father of Modern Bacteriology, introduced solid culture media, aniline dye staining, and discovered CAT (Cholera, Anthrax, Tuberculosis)? {{c1::Robert Koch}}
answer: Also: Formulated Koch's postulates (4 original + 1 immunological).

question: Who is the Father of Chemotherapy, discovered Ehrlichia, standardized toxin-antitoxin, and modified the ZN/acid-fast stain? {{c1::Paul Ehrlich}}

Match the pioneers: {{c1::Joseph Lister}} (antiseptic surgery), {{c2::Antonie van Leeuwenhoek}} (simple light microscope), {{c3::Ernst Ruska}} (electron microscope), {{c4::Edward Jenner}} (smallpox vaccine), {{c5::Kary B. Mullis}} (PCR).
answer: Also: Eva Engvall & Peter Perlman developed ELISA.

question: Which 3 organisms are exceptions to Koch's postulates (LPG)? {{c1::Mycobacterium leprae (grown in armadillo), Treponema pallidum, and Gonococci}}
answer: Reason: Cannot be cultured on artificial cell-free media (M. leprae, T. pallidum) or lack an animal model (Gonococci).

question: In which phase of the bacterial growth curve is there NO increase in bacterial number, but maximum increase in cell size, enzymes, and metabolites? {{c1::Lag phase}}
answer: Key: Maximum cell size is seen at the end of the lag phase.

question: In which phase of the bacterial growth curve does rapid cell division occur with smaller cell size and maximum metabolic activity? {{c1::Log (exponential) phase}}
answer: Clinical: Bacteria are most susceptible to β-lactam antibiotics during the Log phase.

question: Which bacterial growth phase shows equal viable and dead cells and 'STAB' events: {{c1::Sporulation, Exotoxin, Antibiotic, and Bacteriocin}} production? {{c2::Stationary phase}}
Name the 3 modes of horizontal bacterial gene transfer shown: {{c1::Transformation}} (uptake of free DNA), {{c2::Transduction}} (bacteriophage-mediated), and {{c3::Conjugation}} (sex pilus-mediated).
answer: Transformation: Requires competence factor during log phase (e.g., Streptococcus pneumoniae).

question: What is the most common mode of drug resistance transfer in Staphylococcus aureus (mediated by a tadpole-shaped DNA virus)? {{c1::Transduction (via Bacteriophage)}}
answer: Types: Generalized transduction (lytic phage) vs Specialized transduction (lysogenic phage).

question: Identify the gene transfer mechanism shown where a lytic bacteriophage accidentally packages host bacterial DNA and delivers it to a recipient bacterium: {{c1::Generalized Transduction}}.
answer: Contrast: Specialized transduction transfers only genes adjacent to the prophage site.

question: In Dark-field microscopy, thin spirochetes appear {{c1::bright organisms against a dark background}} using a {{c2::dark-field condenser}}.
answer: Classic use: Treponema pallidum showing corkscrew motility.

question: In Phase-contrast microscopy, unstained organisms appear {{c1::dark against a bright background}} using a {{c2::phase plate}}.
answer: Advantage: Visualizes live internal structures and motility without staining.

question: Which microscopy method uses a bright-field microscope to appreciate BOTH bacterial morphology and motility (e.g., corkscrew or darting motility)? {{c1::Wet mount / Hanging drop}}
answer: Note: Fixed/stained smears visualize morphology better but do NOT appreciate motility.

question: Which capsule stain uses {{c1::polychrome methylene blue}} and specifically detects only the {{c2::polypeptide capsule}} of Bacillus anthracis? {{c3::McFadyean's staining}}
answer: Appearance: Purple bacilli with pink/reddish-purple amorphous capsule.

question: Which immunological capsule test demonstrates {{c1::capsular swelling}} when mixed with type-specific antiserum, and works ONLY for {{c2::polysaccharide capsules}}? {{c3::Quellung reaction}}
What is the best and most rapid immunological test for detecting ALL types of bacterial capsular antigens in CSF/serum? {{c1::Latex agglutination test}} (shows clumping).
answer: Screening microscopic test: Negative staining with India ink / Nigrosin.

question: All bacteria possess a peptidoglycan cell wall EXCEPT {{c1::Mycoplasma (Mollicutes)}}.
answer: Consequence: Pleomorphic, Gram-stain negative, intrinsically resistant to β-lactams.

question: Peptidoglycan is combined with {{c1::Teichoic acid}} in GPB, {{c2::Mycolic acid & LAM}} in Mycobacteria, {{c3::LPS}} in GNB, and {{c4::LOS}} in Neisseria.
answer: Fungal cell wall: Made of Chitin (with β-D-glucan).

question: Which bacterial surface appendages serve as organs of attachment (especially in UTI caused by E. coli) and are identified by {{c1::hemagglutination}}? {{c2::Fimbriae / Pili}}
On Nutrient agar, most common bacteria (e.g., E. coli) form {{c1::white-grey colonies}}.
answer: Pigment producers: S. aureus = golden yellow; Pseudomonas = bluish-green.

question: Which organism produces golden-yellow colonies due to {{c1::β-carotene}} pigment on nutrient agar? {{c2::Staphylococcus aureus}}
answer: Note: Pigment production is enhanced on milk agar / nutrient agar at room temperature.

question: On MacConkey agar, {{c1::lactose fermenters}} (E. coli, Klebsiella) produce {{c2::pink colonies}}, whereas non-lactose fermenters produce {{c3::pale colonies}}.
answer: Inhibitor: Bile salts inhibit Gram-positive bacteria.

question: Identify the pale colonies on MacConkey agar shown: {{c1::Non-lactose fermenters}} (e.g., Salmonella, Shigella, Proteus, Pseudomonas).
answer: Composition: Lactose sugar + Neutral red indicator + Bile salts.

question: On CLED agar, lactose fermenters produce {{c1::yellow colonies}}, whereas non-lactose fermenters produce {{c2::blue colonies}}.
answer: Full form: Cysteine-Lactose-Electrolyte-Deficient agar; prevents swarming of Proteus.

question: Identify the blue colonies on CLED agar shown: {{c1::Non-lactose fermenting organisms}}.
answer: Organisms grown: Both Gram-negative, Gram-positive, and Candida (ideal for urine culture).

question: Match enrichment media colors: {{c1::Selenite F broth}} = light brown; {{c2::Tetrathionate broth}} = bluish-green; {{c3::Alkaline peptone water}} = straw-colored (for Vibrio).
Which method is used for sputum liquefaction and decontamination of commensals before mycobacterial testing? {{c1::NALC–NaOH method}} (N-Acetyl-L-cysteine + NaOH).
answer: Role: NALC liquefies sputum; NaOH kills commensals.

question: Which stool transport medium preserves ALL pathogens (preferred over Buffered Glycerol Saline)? {{c1::Cary-Blair medium}}
In {{c1::Thioglycollate broth}}, aerobes grow at the {{c2::top}} while strict anaerobes grow at the {{c3::bottom}}.
answer: Gold standard anaerobic medium: Robertson Cooked Meat (RCM) > Thioglycollate broth.

question: Identify the biochemical test showing coagulum formation (+ve on right): {{c1::Coagulase test}} — positive in {{c2::Staphylococcus aureus}}.
answer: Slide vs Tube: Slide detects bound coagulase (clumping factor); Tube detects free coagulase.

question: Which 3 high-yield bacteria are Urease-positive (turning the medium pink)? {{c1::Helicobacter pylori, Proteus, and Nocardia}}
What are the 3 steps & temperatures of each PCR cycle (repeated 40 times)? {{c1::Denaturation (95°C)}} → {{c2::Annealing (55°C)}} → {{c3::Extension (72°C)}}.
answer: DNA extraction: Uses Lysozyme; Detection: Gel electrophoresis / fluorescent probe.

question: Match PCR types: {{c1::Conventional PCR}} (DNA only), {{c2::Real-time RT-PCR}} (DNA & RNA via reverse transcriptase), {{c3::Multiplex RT-PCR}} (multiple organisms / syndromic), {{c4::CBNAAT / TrueNAT}} (automated cartridge/chip).
answer: CT value: Inversely proportional to organism load.

question: In the Weil-Felix test (heterophile Ab detection), {{c1::OX-K}} is positive in {{c2::Orientia (Scrub typhus)}}, whereas {{c3::OX-2 ± OX-19}} is positive in {{c4::Rickettsia}}.
Identify the most common phenotypic AST method shown on Mueller-Hinton agar: {{c1::Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion}} (measures ZOI, does NOT give MIC).
answer: Interpretation: Larger Zone of Inhibition (ZOI) = Sensitive.

question: Identify the AST method shown on Mueller-Hinton agar that provides BOTH Zone of Inhibition and MIC: {{c1::E-strip (Epsilometer test)}}.
answer: MIC: Read where the elliptical inhibition zone intersects the strip scale.

question: What is the GOLD STANDARD phenotypic AST method (using Mueller-Hinton broth) that measures test tube turbidity to determine MIC? {{c1::Broth dilution}}
answer: Interpretation: Clear tube = Sensitive; Turbid tube = Resistant.

question: Which 2 genital ulcer pathogens show Safety-Pin / Bipolar staining on Wayson's stain? {{c1::Klebsiella granulomatis and Haemophilus ducreyi}}
Name the key obligate intracellular bacteria: {{c1::Rickettsia and Chlamydia}}.
answer: Facultative intracellular: Mycobacterium, Actinomycetes, Neisseria, Salmonella, Brucella, Listeria.

question: Name the key capsulated bacteria: {{c1::Pneumococcus, Meningococcus, Haemophilus influenzae b (Hib), Klebsiella, Bacillus anthracis}}.
answer: Detection: Quellung reaction (polysaccharide) or McFadyean's (B. anthracis polypeptide).

question: Which 4 high-yield bacteria are NON-cultivable on artificial media? {{c1::Rickettsia, Chlamydia, Treponema pallidum, and Mycobacterium leprae}}
Dimorphic fungi grow as {{c1::yeast}} in patient samples / at {{c2::37°C}}, and as {{c3::mould (hyphae)}} in culture at {{c4::25°C}}.
answer: 6 Dimorphic fungi: Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Paracoccidioides, Sporothrix, Talaromyces.

question: {{c1::Aspergillus}} has {{c2::septate}} hyphae with {{c3::acute & dichotomous branching}}, whereas {{c4::Mucorales (Rhizopus, Absidia, Mucor)}} have {{c5::aseptate}} hyphae with {{c6::obtuse & perpendicular branching}}.

Match asexual fungal spores: {{c1::Arthrospores}} (Dermatophyte, Coccidioides, Trichosporon), {{c2::Blastospores}} (Yeast & yeast-like), {{c3::Chlamydospores}} (Candida), {{c4::Conidiospores}} (Septate mould), {{c5::Sporangiospores}} (Aseptate mould).
Name the two nucleic acid paradox viruses: {{c1::Parvovirus}} is the only {{c2::ssDNA}} virus, and {{c3::Rotavirus}} is the classic {{c4::dsRNA}} virus.
answer: Size extremes: Largest = Poxvirus; Smallest = Parvovirus.

question: Name the 3 Enveloped DNA virus families (HHP): {{c1::Hepadnavirus (HBV), Herpesvirus (HHV), and Poxvirus}}.
Name the 5 Non-enveloped RNA virus families (PC-HAR): {{c1::Picorna (HAV, Polio, Coxsackie, Entero), Calici (Noro, Sapo), Hepe (HEV), Astro, Reo (Rota)}}.
Identify the segmented RNA viruses: {{c1::Influenza virus}} has {{c2::8 segments}}, whereas {{c3::Rotavirus}} has {{c4::11 segments}}.
answer: Copies: HIV has 2 identical ssRNA copies.

question: Compare circular DNA viruses: {{c1::HBV}} has {{c2::partially double-stranded circular DNA}}, whereas {{c3::HPV}} has {{c4::completely double-stranded circular DNA}}.
answer: Shapes: Pox = Box; Rabies = Bullet; Ebola = Filamentous.

question: Match viral shapes: {{c1::Poxvirus}} = Box/Brick-shaped; {{c2::Rabies virus}} = Bullet-shaped; {{c3::Ebola virus}} = Filamentous.
answer: Diagnosis: Electron microscopy visualizes viruses; Bright-field visualizes inclusion bodies.

question: Intranuclear inclusions: {{c1::HSV}} (Cowdry type A / Lipschütz), {{c2::CMV}} (Owl-eye), {{c3::Yellow Fever}} (Torres / Councilman bodies). Intracytoplasmic inclusion: {{c4::Rabies}} (Negri bodies).
answer: Culture ID: Direct Fluorescent Antibody (DFA) is M/C.

question: Name the 4 free-living amoebae (soil & water, pseudopodia +ve): {{c1::Naegleria, Acanthamoeba, Balamuthia, and Sappinia}}.

Match protozoal immunological tests: {{c1::Leishmania}} = Rapid test detecting Ab against {{c2::rK39 Ag}}; {{c3::P. vivax}} = pLDH Ag; {{c4::P. falciparum}} = pLDH + {{c5::HRP-2 Ag}}; {{c6::Toxoplasma}} = {{c7::Sabin-Feldman dye test}} (IgG).
answer: Sample: Intestinal = stool; Free-living = CSF; Blood/tissue = PBS/biopsy.

question: Match cestodes & intermediate/definitive hosts: {{c1::T. solium}} (Pork), {{c2::T. saginata}} (Beef), {{c3::H. nana}} (Dwarf, only man), {{c4::D. latum}} (Fish/cyclops), {{c5::Echinococcus granulosus}} (Dog).
Which 3 helminths infect humans by {{c1::skin penetration}}? {{c2::Schistosoma (trematode), Strongyloides, and Ancylostoma (nematodes)}}.
answer: Infective eggs: Echinococcus, H. nana, Ascaris, Trichuris, Enterobius.

question: Visceral Larva Migrans: Human = {{c1::Ascaris lumbricoides}}, Animal (M/C) = {{c2::Toxocara canis}}. Cutaneous Larva Migrans: Human = {{c3::Strongyloides (Larva currens) & Ancylostoma duodenale}}, Animal (M/C) = {{c4::Ancylostoma braziliense / caninum}}.

List the 6 WHO steps of hand hygiene: (1) Palm to palm, (2) {{c1::Back of hand with interlaced fingers}}, (3) {{c2::Palm to palm interlaced}}, (4) {{c3::Backs of fingers/knuckles to opposing palms}}, (5) {{c4::Thumb rotational}}, (6) {{c5::Tips of fingers circularly on palm}}.
PPE Donning sequence: {{c1::Hand hygiene → Gown → Mask → Goggles/Face shield → Gloves}}. Doffing sequence: {{c2::Gloves → Gown → Goggles/Face shield → Mask → Hand hygiene}}.
answer: Rule: Remove the most contaminated item (gloves) first, and perform hand hygiene last.

question: Complete killing of all forms of microorganisms INCLUDING spores is {{c1::Sterilization}}, whereas EXCLUDING spores is {{c2::Disinfection}}.
answer: Thermal indicators: Autoclave = 121°C, 15 min, 15 psi; Hot air oven = 160°C, 2 hours.

question: Match sterilization methods: Surgical instruments & rigid endoscopes = {{c1::Autoclave > H2O2 > ETO}}; Glass & sharps = {{c2::Autoclave > Hot air oven}}; Oily/powdery materials = {{c3::Hot air oven}}; Serum/Egg culture media (Loeffler's, LJ) = {{c4::Inspissation > Tyndallization}}.

High-level disinfectant (kills some spores): {{c1::Aldehyde (Glutaraldehyde > OPA)}}. Intermediate-level (kills M. tuberculosis): {{c2::1% Na hypochlorite, alcohol}}. Low-level (does NOT kill M. tb): {{c3::Benzalkonium chloride}}.
answer: Flexible endoscopes: Glutaraldehyde > OPA > H2O2 > ETO. Blood spill: 1% Na hypochlorite.

question: Match disinfectant efficacy tests: {{c1::Chick-Martin}} (in presence of organic matter), {{c2::Rideal-Walker}} (in absence of organic matter), {{c3::Kelsey-Sykes}} (capacity test), {{c4::Maurer's In-use}} (contamination).

Active acquired immunity (antigen entry → antibody production): {{c1::Infection & Vaccination}}. Passive acquired immunity (antibodies directly received): {{c2::Maternal IgG, Post-exposure prophylaxis IgG, Blood transfusion IgG}}.

T-cell activation requires 3 signals: (1) Ag presentation ({{c1::MHC-I to CD8 TCR}} or {{c2::MHC-II to CD4 TCR}}), (2) Co-stimulatory ({{c3::B7 on APC to CD28 on T-cell}}), (3) Cytokine ({{c4::IL-1 / IL-2}}).
Unlike normal antigens (bound in the peptide groove), {{c1::Superantigens}} (TSST, S. aureus enterotoxin) bind to the {{c2::lateral side of the β-chain}} of MHC-II and TCR.
answer: Result: Massive non-specific T-cell activation & cytokine storm (Toxic shock syndrome).

question: In primary vs secondary immune response, antibody production occurs in the {{c1::germinal centre of lymph nodes}} in order: {{c2::IgM > IgG > IgA > IgE}}.
answer: Mechanisms: Somatic hypermutation + Affinity maturation + Class/isotype switching.

question: Which immunoglobulin has the highest serum concentration, persists for years, and crosses the placenta? {{c1::IgG}} (Subclass {{c2::IgG1}} is M/C; {{c3::IgG2}} acts against capsulated organisms).
answer: IgM: Pentamer, highest molecular weight, fixes complement.

question: Compare {{c1::Secretory IgA}} (dimer, mucosal local immunity in RT, GIT, GUT, breast milk) vs {{c2::IgD}} (B-cell receptor with IgM) vs {{c3::IgE}} (elevated in Type 1 hypersensitivity & parasitic infections).
answer: Complement fixation: IgM, IgG, and Serum IgA fix complement.

question: Which Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL) is {{c1::Type 3 (immune complex)}} hypersensitivity, whereas Type 1 lepra reaction is {{c2::Type 4 (delayed)}} hypersensitivity?
answer: Note: Most reactions with 'reaction' or 'test' (Mantoux, Lepromin) are Type 4, except Arthus/Type 2 lepra (Type 3).

question: In Host-vs-Graft Disease (allograft rejection): Hyperacute (hours) = {{c1::Humoral / Type 2 HSR}}; Acute (months) & Chronic (years) = {{c2::Cell-mediated / Type 4 HSR}}.
answer: GVHD: Seen with bone marrow or thymus allografts (Type 4 CMI).

question: Combined IDD: {{c1::SCID}} (X-linked IL-R gene M/C; AR ADA deficiency), {{c2::Wiskott-Aldrich}} (X-linked, WAS gene), {{c3::Ataxia telangiectasia}} (AR, ATM DNA repair defect).
answer: Cellular IDD: DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion → CATCH defects).

question: Compare phagocytic IDDs: {{c1::CGD}} (X-linked Phox/NADPH oxidase defect, ↑catalase +ve S. aureus infections, NBT & DHR +ve) vs {{c2::Chediak-Higashi}} (AR LYST defect in phagosome-lysosome fusion, albinism + peroxidase +ve giant granules).

Complement deficiencies: {{c1::C1, C4, C2}} → SLE; {{c2::C3}} → Glomerulonephritis; {{c3::C5b–C9 (MAC)}} → Disseminated Neisseria; {{c4::C1 esterase inhibitor}} → Hereditary angioneurotic edema; {{c5::DAF}} → PNH; {{c6::Factor I/H}} → Immune complex diseases.
Identify the meningeal sign shown where passive neck flexion causes involuntary flexion of hips and knees: {{c1::Brudzinski's sign}}.
answer: Neck rigidity: Difficulty in neck flexion.

question: Acute bacterial meningitis M/C causes: Adults = {{c1::Pneumococcus}} (Meningococcus causes bleeding rashes in North India); Children = {{c2::H. influenzae b}}; Neonates = {{c3::Group B Strep}} (world) / {{c4::E. coli}} (India) / {{c5::Listeria}}.
Identify the CSF Gram stain showing intracellular lens-shaped Gram-negative diplococci inside neutrophils: {{c1::Neisseria meningitidis}}.
answer: Culture & Biochem: Thayer-Martin medium; ferments BOTH glucose & maltose.

question: Identify the CSF Gram stain showing lancet/lens-shaped Gram-positive cocci in pairs: {{c1::Streptococcus pneumoniae}}.
answer: Tests: α-hemolysis, Optochin sensitive, Bile soluble, Inulin fermenter.

question: Identify the Blood agar phenomenon shown where H. influenzae b grows as tiny colonies around a streak of S. aureus: {{c1::Satellitism}}.
answer: Reason: S. aureus provides Factor V (NAD), while blood agar provides Factor X (Hemin).

question: Which neonatal meningitis GPB shows {{c1::tumbling motility at 22°C}} (room temp) and is {{c2::non-motile at 37°C}}? {{c3::Listeria monocytogenes}}
In Chronic Bacterial Meningitis (M. tuberculosis), CSF shows ↑↑↑Proteins with {{c1::cobweb formation}}, and microscopy shows {{c2::acid-fast non-filamentous bacilli}}.
DNA viral encephalitis: {{c1::HSV-1}} causes M/C sporadic {{c2::temporal lobe encephalitis}} (Rx Acyclovir); {{c3::JC virus}} causes {{c4::PML (white brain disease)}} in immunocompromised patients.

RNA viral encephalitis: {{c1::Japanese Encephalitis}} (M/C, children 5–15 yrs, Northern India, {{c2::Culex mosquito}}, live SA-14-14-2 / killed Kolar vaccine) and {{c3::Nipah virus}} (West Bengal/Kerala, {{c4::Fruit bat}}).
Rabies (100% mortality, hydrophobia; World vector = Bat, India = Dog): Best diagnostic test = {{c1::PCR on Saliva > CSF}} or {{c2::DFA on skin (nape of neck) > cornea}}.
answer: PEP (4 steps): (1) Wash soap & water, (2) Antiseptics, (3) Ig, (4) Killed vaccine in deltoid.

question: 7–10 years after primary Measles (Fever → Koplik spots → Rash), reactivation causes {{c1::SSPE (Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis)}} with ↓school performance & {{c2::myoclonus}}.
Identify the free-living amoeba causing acute {{c1::PAM (Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis)}} with {{c2::lobe-like pseudopodia}}: {{c3::Naegleria fowleri}}.
Identify the free-living amoeba with {{c1::spike/thorn-like pseudopodia}} causing chronic {{c2::GAE}} and {{c3::contact lens keratitis}}: {{c4::Acanthamoeba}}.
answer: Contrast: Sappinia has bilobed nucleus; Balamuthia has branching pseudopodia.

question: Identify the free-living amoeba with {{c1::branching pseudopodia}} causing chronic granulomatous amoebic encephalitis (GAE): {{c2::Balamuthia}}.
answer: Sappinia: Subacute SAE, trophozoite has bilobed nucleus.

question: Tetanus PEP: If ≥3 previous TT doses: clean wound needs Td if last dose ≥{{c1::10 years}}, dirty wound if ≥{{c2::5 years}}. If <3/unknown doses: clean needs complete Td; dirty needs {{c3::complete Td + Immunoglobulins}}.
answer: Toxin: Tetanospasmin inhibits Glycine & GABA → spastic paralysis.

question: Identify the painless vascular bleeding spots on palms/soles in Infective Endocarditis: {{c1::Janeway lesions}}.
answer: Contrast: Osler's nodes = painful immunological nodules on finger/toe pads.

question: Identify the painful immunological nodules on fingers/palms/soles in Infective Endocarditis: {{c1::Osler's nodes}}.
answer: Also immunological: Roth's spots (retinal hemorrhages with pale center).

question: Identify the retinal bleeding spots seen in Infective Endocarditis: {{c1::Roth's spots}}.
answer: Etiology: Native = S. aureus; Early prosthetic (<1 yr) = S. epidermidis; Late (>1 yr) = S. viridans.

question: Updated Modified Duke's Major Criteria (3): (1) Positive blood culture (≥2 typical, ≥3 atypical, or {{c1::1 Coxiella}}), (2) {{c2::Coxiella/Bartonella PCR or IgG ≥ 1:800}}, (3) Imaging ({{c3::ECHO/CT vegetation/dehiscence}} or {{c4::FDG PET/CT > 3 months}}), plus surgical evidence.
answer: Minor criteria: Fever >38°C, FDG PET/CT <3 mo, predisposing factors, Janeway, Osler/Roth, new murmur.

question: Empirical/standard IE treatment: {{c1::Penicillin + Gentamicin + Rifampicin}} (or {{c2::Vancomycin}} if penicillin-allergic); duration is {{c3::4–6 weeks}} for native valve and {{c4::6 weeks}} for prosthetic valve.
answer: Note: S. epidermidis is M/C early prosthetic IE.

question: In Modified Jones criteria for ARF: High-risk populations count {{c1::monoarthritis}} (major), fever {{c2::≥ 38°C}}, monoarthralgia, and ESR {{c3::≥ 30 mm/hr}}; Low-risk requires {{c4::polyarthritis}}, fever ≥ 38.5°C, polyarthralgia, ESR ≥ 60 mm/hr.
In the HIV virion: {{c1::env}} encodes gp120 & gp41 (glycosylated envelope complex); {{c2::gag}} encodes p24 capsid; {{c3::pol}} encodes reverse transcriptase, integrase, and protease.

HIV WHO Staging: Stage 1 = asymptomatic/PGL; Stage 2 = aphthous ulcers/herpes zoster; Stage 3 = {{c1::oral candidiasis/hairy leukoplakia, pulmonary TB, >1 mo fever/diarrhoea}}; Stage 4 (AIDS) = {{c2::oesophageal candidiasis, wasting, extrapulmonary TB, Kaposi's sarcoma}}.
answer: Oral test: Scrapes off = Candida; Not removed = Oral hairy leukoplakia (EBV).

question: NACO adult HIV diagnosis (post 3 wk–3 mo window): 3 rapid/ELISA tests — {{c1::2 +ve}} if symptomatic, {{c2::3 +ve}} if asymptomatic. Congenital HIV: {{c3::Dried blood spot PCR}} at {{c4::6 wks, 6 mo, 12 mo}} → Ab at {{c5::18 months}}.
Why is secondary Dengue infection much more severe (DHF / DSS) than primary infection? {{c1::ADE (Antibody-Dependent Enhancement)}}.

Compare VHF: {{c1::Lassa & Hanta}} cause VHF + pneumonia (absent in India); {{c2::CCHF}} is transmitted by {{c3::Ixodid tick}} (seen in Gujarat); {{c4::Ebola & Marburg}} have {{c5::fruit bat}} reservoir and cause VHF + septic shock.
Identify the malaria RBC stippling shown with smooth, fine dots and brown pigment: {{c1::Schuffner's dots (Plasmodium vivax)}}.
answer: Antigen: pLDH only; Rx: Chloroquine + Primaquine (prevents relapse).

question: Identify the malaria PBS showing multiple ring trophozoites inside single RBCs: {{c1::Plasmodium falciparum}}.
answer: Antigens: pLDH + HRP-2; Schizonts are NOT seen in PBS (sequestered in capillaries).

question: Identify the banana/sickle-shaped gametocyte shown in PBS: {{c1::Plasmodium falciparum}}.
answer: Pigment & clefts: Maurer's clefts (rough, bigger) + black pigment.

question: Identify the rough, larger RBC clefts with black pigment shown in P. falciparum: {{c1::Maurer's clefts}}.
answer: Complications: Cerebral malaria, Blackwater fever, Algid malaria, ATN.

question: Drug-resistant P. falciparum Rx: Artesunate + Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine + Primaquine (kills gametocytes); North-East India = {{c1::Artemether + Lumefantrine}}; Pregnancy 1st tri = {{c2::Quinine}}, 2nd/3rd tri = {{c3::Artesunate}}.
Identify the tick-borne intraerythrocytic parasite showing single ring trophozoites (often confused with P. falciparum) and Maltese cross tetrads: {{c1::Babesia}}.
