question: Name the 7 high-yield Gram-positive bacilli: {{c1::Bacillus, Clostridium, Corynebacterium, Mycobacterium, Actinomycetes, Nocardia, Listeria}}.
Gram-positive cocci: {{c1::Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Pneumococcus, Enterococcus}}. Gram-negative cocci: {{c2::Meningococcus, Gonococcus}}.
Name the 7 Enterobacteriaceae genera: {{c1::Escherichia, Klebsiella, Salmonella, Shigella, Yersinia, Proteus, Citrobacter}}.
answer: Key: All are Gram-negative bacilli, oxidase-negative, catalase-positive, glucose fermenters.

question: Name the 7 Oxidase-positive Gram-negative bacilli: {{c1::Vibrio, Pseudomonas, Campylobacter, Helicobacter, Haemophilus (Hib), Brucella, Bordetella}}.
Miscellaneous Gram-negative bacilli: {{c1::HACEK group}} (culture-negative endocarditis), {{c2::Acinetobacter}} (VAP), and {{c3::Gardnerella vaginalis}} (bacterial vaginosis Clue cells).

Compare {{c1::HSV-1 (HHV-1)}} (upper body vesicles, sporadic temporal lobe encephalitis) vs {{c2::HSV-2 (HHV-2)}} (lower body vesicles, genital ulcers, neonatal Mollaret's meningitis) vs {{c3::VZV (HHV-3)}} (entire body, chickenpox/shingles).

Match HHV diseases: {{c1::HHV-4 (EBV)}} = IMN, Burkitt's & Hodgkin's lymphoma, nasopharyngeal/gastric Ca; {{c2::HHV-5 (CMV)}} = IMN, post-transplant <3 mo; {{c3::HHV-8}} = Kaposi's sarcoma (M/C cancer in HIV).
answer: EBV & CMV Dx: ELISA (exception among HHVs, which use PCR).

question: Compare Poxviruses: {{c1::Smallpox}} (severe septic shock, live vaccine), {{c2::Monkeypox}} (moderate), {{c3::Vaccinia}} (mild), {{c4::Molluscum contagiosum}} (mild, ALL papules umbilicated, NO vaccine).
During the HBV window period (when HBsAg and Anti-HBs are both negative), which marker confirms acute HBV infection? {{c1::IgM Anti-HBc}}
Which lung fluke is oviparous with an {{c1::operculated egg with abopercular thickening}} found in BOTH {{c2::stool and sputum}}? {{c3::Paragonimus westermani}} (Rx Praziquantel).
Identify the liver fluke egg shown (operculated, in stool): {{c1::Fasciola hepatica}} (hosts: man, snail, aquatic plants; causes hepatitis & cholangitis; Rx {{c2::Triclabendazole}}).
Identify the largest intestinal fluke (trematode) whose operculated egg is seen in stool: {{c1::Fasciola buski}} (Rx Praziquantel).
answer: Hosts: Man, snail, aquatic plants.

question: Identify the dwarf tapeworm egg shown with {{c1::inner & outer membranes and polar filaments}}: {{c2::Hymenolepis nana}} (only human host, autoinfective, non-bile stained).
Identify the muscle biopsy showing a {{c1::coiled spiral larva}} (accompanied by myalgia, myocarditis, and Bachman test +ve): {{c2::Trichinella spiralis}} (Rx Albendazole).
Identify the subcutaneous fungal infection showing brown {{c1::Medlar / Sclerotic / Copper-penny bodies}} on microscopy: {{c2::Chromoblastomycosis (Cladosporium)}}.
answer: Clinical: Verrucous wart-like nodules; brown/black pigment on SDA.

question: Compare Madura foot: {{c1::Eumycetoma (Madurella mycetomatis)}} has {{c2::black granules}} (fungal, Rx Itraconazole), whereas {{c3::Actinomycetoma (Nocardia/Actinomadura)}} has {{c4::whitish-yellow granules}} (bacterial, Rx Welsh regimen).
Identify the annular, red, scaly, itchy skin lesion shown: {{c1::Tinea corporis (Ringworm)}} — M/C cause = {{c2::Trichophyton rubrum}} (produces red pigment on SDA).
answer: Rx: Topical Ketoconazole/Clotrimazole or Oral Itraconazole/Fluconazole.

question: Identify the superficial fungal infection showing {{c1::hypopigmented patches on the upper trunk}}: {{c2::Tinea/Pityriasis versicolor (Malassezia globosa)}}.
answer: KOH mount: Spaghetti & meatball appearance; Wood's lamp = golden yellow.

question: Identify the slit-skin smear finding shown with acid-fast bacilli arranged in {{c1::cigar bundles / globi}}: {{c2::Mycobacterium leprae}}.
answer: Sample site: Earlobe / elbow; Non-cultivable.

question: Identify the {{c1::sunray appearance}} of crushed sulphur granule shown: {{c2::Actinomyces}} (anaerobic, non-acid-fast, causes lumpy jaw; Rx Penicillin).
Identify the Gram stain showing chains of Gram-positive bacilli with non-bulging spores ({{c1::bamboo stick appearance}}): {{c2::Bacillus anthracis}}.
answer: Culture on Blood agar: Medusa head / String of pearls appearance.

question: Identify the urethral smear showing {{c1::kidney-shaped Gram-negative diplococci inside neutrophils}}: {{c2::Neisseria gonorrhoeae}}.
answer: Culture & Rx: Thayer-Martin medium; non-maltose fermenter; Rx Ceftriaxone.

question: Identify the microscopy of curdy-white vaginal discharge showing {{c1::budding yeast with pseudohyphae}}: {{c2::Candida albicans}} (Rx Fluconazole).
answer: Itching: Severe (vs mild in Trichomonas, none in Gardnerella).

question: Identify the wheel-shaped viral gastroenteritis pathogen with {{c1::11 segments of dsRNA}} (M/C in children < 2 yrs): {{c2::Rotavirus}}.
answer: Dx: Stool Antigen ELISA; Live oral vaccine.

question: Identify the GMS-stained BAL specimen showing {{c1::crushed ping-pong ball / black cysts}}: {{c2::Pneumocystis jirovecii}} (CD4 < 200; Rx Cotrimoxazole).
Identify the narrow septate hyphae with {{c1::acute-angle dichotomous branching}}: {{c2::Aspergillus}} (Rx Voriconazole).
Identify the India-ink negative stain showing a clear {{c1::capsular halo}} around budding yeast: {{c2::Cryptococcus neoformans}} (causes meningitis in HIV).
answer: Culture: Bird seed agar (brown melanin colonies).

question: Identify the PBS showing {{c1::spindle-shaped trypomastigotes with folded undulating flagella}}: {{c2::Trypanosoma}} (T. cruzi = Chagas; T. brucei = Sleeping sickness).
answer: Vectors: Reduviid bug (Chagas); Tse-tse fly (Sleeping sickness).

question: Identify the PBS showing {{c1::amastigote LD bodies with kinetoplast}} inside a macrophage: {{c2::Leishmania donovani}} (Kala-azar).
answer: Vector: Sandfly (Phlebotomus); Rx: Liposomal Amphotericin B / Miltefosine.

question: Identify the RBC merozoites arranged in a {{c1::Maltese cross (tetrad)}}: {{c2::Babesia microti}} (Ixodid tick; Rx Atovaquone ± Azithromycin).
answer: Presentation: Fever, chills, myalgia, hemolytic anemia.

question: Identify the urine microscopy egg with a {{c1::terminal spine}}: {{c2::Schistosoma haematobium}} (causes painless hematuria & {{c3::bladder carcinoma}}).
Identify the sheathed microfilaria with {{c1::no nuclei in the tail tip}}: {{c2::Wuchereria bancrofti}} (M/C cause of lymphatic filariasis / elephantiasis in India).
Identify the vector shown ({{c1::Rat flea / Xenopsylla cheopis}}), which transmits {{c2::Plague (Yersinia pestis)}} and {{c3::Endemic typhus (Rickettsia typhi)}}.
Identify the vector shown ({{c1::Louse}}), which transmits {{c2::Epidemic typhus (R. prowazekii), Epidemic relapsing fever (B. recurrentis), and Trench fever (Bartonella quintana)}}.
Identify the vector shown ({{c1::Soft tick / Argasid tick}}), which transmits {{c2::Endemic relapsing fever (Borrelia duttoni)}} and {{c3::Q fever (Coxiella burnetii)}}.
answer: Q fever M/C route: Inhalation.

question: Identify the vector shown ({{c1::Mite / Trombiculid chigger}}), which transmits {{c2::Scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi — black eschar)}} and {{c3::Rickettsial pox (R. akari)}}.
answer: Weil-Felix: OX-K positive in Scrub typhus.

question: Staphylococcus aureus is the M/C cause of which 5 clinical conditions? {{c1::Abscess, Burn wound infection, Native valve IE, Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP), and Osteomyelitis}}.
Which Beta-hemolytic Group B Streptococcus is {{c1::CAMP test +ve}} and causes {{c2::Neonatal sepsis & Neonatal meningitis}}? {{c3::Streptococcus agalactiae}}
Bacillus anthracis causes {{c1::Cutaneous anthrax / Hide porter's disease}} (malignant pustule → black eschar) and {{c2::Pulmonary anthrax / Wool sorter's disease}} (hemorrhagic pneumonia).
What is the M/C cause of Actinomycetoma in the world vs in India? World = {{c1::Nocardia}}; India = {{c2::Actinomadura}}.
Malassezia investigations: Wood's lamp = {{c1::golden-yellow fluorescence}}; KOH mount = {{c2::spaghetti & meatball appearance}}; Urease = {{c3::+ve}}.

Dermatophyte investigations: Wood's lamp = {{c1::apple-green fluorescence}}; Hair perforation test +ve = {{c2::Trichophyton mentagrophytes}}; M/C skin/nail species = {{c3::T. rubrum (red pigment on SDA)}}.
Which subcutaneous dematiaceous fungal infection is caused by {{c1::Bipolaris}} and shows NO Medlar/sclerotic bodies (unlike Chromoblastomycosis)? {{c2::Phaeohyphomycosis}}
Toxoplasma gondii transmission: Cat passes {{c1::oocyst in stool}} → sporulation in soil → {{c2::sporulated oocyst (infective form)}} → feco-oral route to humans.
Name the 3 viviparous nematodes (lay larvae directly, no eggs): {{c1::Filarial worms, Trichinella spiralis, and Dracunculus medinensis}}.
Which 6 helminth eggs float in saturated salt solution? {{c1::Trichuris, Enterobius, H. nana, Ancylostoma, Necator, Ascaris}}.
Which 4 helminth eggs are NON-bile-stained (NEHA)? {{c1::Necator, Enterobius, H. nana, Ancylostoma}}.
answer: All other common helminth eggs (Ascaris, Trichuris, Taenia, etc.) are bile-stained.

question: Which 4 helminths can cause autoinfection in humans? Cestodes = {{c1::Taenia solium, H. nana}}; Nematodes = {{c2::Enterobius, Strongyloides}}.

Diagnostic samples in Helminthology: Adult worm from ruptured blister = {{c1::Dracunculus medinensis}}; Larvae in PBS/muscle biopsy = {{c2::Filaria / Trichinella}}; Larvae in stool = {{c3::Strongyloides}}.
answer: Oviparous helminths: Diagnosed by eggs in stool.

question: Dengue lab diagnosis by symptom duration: {{c1::< 5 days}} → detect virus ({{c2::PCR / NS1 Ag}}); {{c3::≥ 5 days}} → detect {{c4::IgM/IgG Antibody}}.
answer: General viral rule: <1 wk = virus (PCR/Ag); >1 wk = Antibody.

question: Compare viral quantification assays: {{c1::Pock assay}} uses {{c2::Chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) of embryonated egg}}, whereas {{c3::Plaque assay}} (M/C) uses {{c4::cell/tissue culture}}.
answer: Culture ID: Direct Fluorescent Antibody (DFA) & Cytopathic effect.

question: Match viral Cytopathic Effects (CPE): Measles = {{c1::Syncytium}}; Adenovirus = {{c2::Granular clumping / bunch of grapes}}; HSV = {{c3::Ballooning}}; Enterovirus = {{c4::Crenation}}.
answer: Live cells required for all viral cultures.

question: Which 3 enteric viruses are routinely diagnosed by {{c1::stool Antigen detection (HAR)}}? {{c2::HBV (actually HAV/HEV?), Adenovirus, and Rotavirus}} — Marrow HAR mnemonic: {{c3::HBV, Adeno, Rota}}.
answer: Ab detection (HPR-JWM): Hepatitis, Herpes, HIV, Hanta, Parvo, Rubella, JE, West Nile, Measles.

question: Enveloped RNA viruses (Part 1): Retro ({{c1::HIV}}), Flavi ({{c2::HCV, JE, YF, KFD, Dengue, West Nile, Zika}}), Toga ({{c3::Chikungunya}}), Matona ({{c4::Rubella}}).
Enveloped RNA viruses (Part 2): Arena ({{c1::Lassa}}), Bunya ({{c2::Hanta, CCHF}}), Orthomyxo ({{c3::Influenza}}), Paramyxo ({{c4::Parainfluenza, Measles, Nipah, Mumps}}), Pneumo ({{c5::RSV, hMPV}}).
Name the 4 Non-enveloped DNA virus families (PPAP): {{c1::Papilloma (HPV), Polyoma (JC, BK), Adenovirus, and Parvovirus}}.
Which immunological antigen-detection test demonstrates toxin production in Corynebacterium diphtheriae? {{c1::Elek's gel precipitation test}}
Which immunological test detects alpha-toxin (lecithinase) production by Clostridium perfringens on egg-yolk agar? {{c1::Nagler's reaction}}
answer: Inhibited by: Specific antitoxin on half the plate.

question: Match agglutination tests: {{c1::Widal}} = Salmonella; {{c2::SAT (Standard Agglutination Test)}} = Brucella; {{c3::MAT (Microscopic Agglutination Test)}} = Leptospira.
CBNAAT (Cartridge-Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test) detects M. tuberculosis and {{c1::rpoB gene}} mutations conferring resistance to {{c2::Rifampicin}}.
Epstein-Barr Virus (HHV-4) causes {{c1::Infectious Mononucleosis (IMN)}}, {{c2::Gastric & Nasopharyngeal carcinoma}}, and {{c3::Burkitt's & Hodgkin's lymphoma}}.
answer: Dx: ELISA (Ab detection); also causes Oral hairy leukoplakia in HIV.

question: Post-transplant infection < 3 months is M/C due to {{c1::CMV (HHV-5)}}, whereas post-transplant nephropathy > 3 months is M/C due to {{c2::BK virus (Polyomavirus)}}.
Which Poxvirus causes mild pearly {{c1::umbilicated papules}} with NO available vaccine? {{c2::Molluscum contagiosum virus}}
Which asexual fungal spore is formed specifically by {{c1::Candida}} under special conditions? {{c2::Chlamydospores}}
Compare invasive fungal serum markers: {{c1::β-D-Glucan}} is positive in Candida, Aspergillus, Pneumocystis, whereas {{c2::Galactomannan}} is specific for {{c3::Aspergillus}}.
Which 3 opportunistic protozoa are {{c1::Acid-Fast}} on modified ZN stain? {{c2::Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora, and Cystoisospora}}.
Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) is endemic in {{c1::Bihar}} and transmitted by the {{c2::Sandfly (Phlebotomus)}}.

Compare Trypanosomiasis: {{c1::Chagas (T. cruzi)}} → Reduviid bug, mega-esophagus/heart/colon, Romana's sign, Rx Benznidazole; {{c2::Sleeping sickness (T. brucei)}} → Tse-tse fly, Winterbottom sign, Rx Suramin.
Identify the P. vivax stage shown in PBS (round with merozoites, NOT seen in P. falciparum PBS): {{c1::Schizont}}.
answer: P. falciparum schizonts remain attached to capillary endothelium.

question: Identify the P. vivax stage shown (single large amoeboid ring form inside enlarged RBC): {{c1::Trophozoite}}.
answer: Contrast: P. falciparum shows multiple small rings per RBC.

question: Identify the round gametocyte shown in PBS: {{c1::Plasmodium vivax}}.
answer: Contrast: P. falciparum gametocyte is banana/sickle-shaped.

question: Identify the trophozoite with pseudopodia and ingested RBCs causing amoebic dysentery & flask-shaped ulcers: {{c1::Entamoeba histolytica}}.
answer: Cyst carriers Rx: Diloxanide furoate / Paromomycin.

question: Identify the oval stool cyst with 4 nuclei shown: {{c1::Giardia lamblia}}.
answer: Trophozoite: Falling-leaf motility, 2 suckers, 8 flagella.

question: Identify the small (4–5 μm) round acid-fast oocysts causing autoinfection & watery diarrhoea in HIV: {{c1::Cryptosporidium}} (Rx {{c2::Nitazoxanide}}).
answer: Size: Smallest of the 3 acid-fast coccidia.

question: Identify the round (8–10 μm) acid-fast oocyst causing traveller's/prolonged diarrhoea: {{c1::Cyclospora}} (Rx {{c2::Cotrimoxazole}}).
Identify the {{c1::acid-fast}} Taenia egg (beef tapeworm) shown: {{c2::Taenia saginata}} (does NOT cause neurocysticercosis).
Identify the large β-hemolytic colonies on Blood agar shown (Coagulase +ve): {{c1::Staphylococcus aureus}}.
Identify the Gram stain showing Gram-positive cocci in chains (Catalase -ve, Bacitracin sensitive): {{c1::Streptococcus pyogenes}}.
Identify the Gram-positive filamentous branching bacilli shown: {{c1::Nocardia}} (acid-fast, aerobic, Madura foot).
Identify the non-acid-fast stain of crushed granules from lumpy jaw: {{c1::Actinomyces}} (anaerobic, Rx Penicillin).
Identify the Tinea capitis lesion showing yellow cup-like crusts ({{c1::Scutula}}): {{c2::Favus (Trichophyton schoenleinii)}}.
Identify the Tinea capitis lesion showing grey patch alopecia with arthroconidia {{c1::outside the hair shaft}}: {{c2::Ectothrix (Microsporum canis)}}.
answer: M/c cause of Tinea capitis overall.

question: Identify the Tinea capitis lesion showing grey patch with {{c1::black dots}} (arthroconidia inside hair shaft): {{c2::Endothrix (Trichophyton tonsurans)}}.
Identify the {{c1::pencil-shaped}} macroconidia shown: {{c2::Trichophyton}} (M/C dermatophyte genus).
Identify the {{c1::club-shaped}} macroconidia shown (lacks microconidia, spares hair): {{c2::Epidermophyton}}.
Identify the mould-phase {{c1::flower-like / daisy-like conidia}} arrangement at 25°C: {{c2::Sporothrix schenckii}}.
answer: Yeast phase (37°C): Cigar-shaped yeast & asteroid bodies.

question: Identify the yeast-phase {{c1::asteroid body}} (Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon) shown: {{c2::Sporothrix schenckii}}.
answer: Clinical: Nodular lymphangitis along lymphatics.

question: Identify the LPCB mount showing conidia covering the {{c1::upper 1/3rd of the vesicle}}: {{c2::Aspergillus fumigatus}} (M/C species).
answer: 2/3rd vesicle: A. flavus; Complete vesicle: A. niger.

question: Identify the LPCB mount showing conidia covering {{c1::2/3rd of the vesicle}}: {{c2::Aspergillus flavus}}.
Identify the Gram/microscopy showing {{c1::budding yeast with pseudohyphae}}: {{c2::Candida}}.
answer: Germ tube +ve: C. albicans & C. dubliniensis.

question: Identify the microscopy of encapsulated {{c1::budding yeast}} without pseudohyphae: {{c2::Cryptococcus neoformans}}.
answer: Bird seed agar: Brown colonies (melanin).

question: Identify the Blood agar showing greenish {{c1::α-hemolysis}} by optochin-sensitive diplococci: {{c2::Pneumococcus}}.
Identify the Blood agar showing clear {{c1::β-hemolysis}} by coagulase-positive cocci: {{c2::Staphylococcus aureus}}.
Identify the Gram stain of {{c1::Gram-positive cocci in clusters}}: {{c2::Staphylococcus aureus}}.
Identify the Gram stain of {{c1::Gram-negative coccobacilli}} in a thumbprint pattern: {{c2::Bordetella pertussis}}.
Identify the Ziehl-Neelsen stain showing {{c1::pink acid-fast, non-filamentous bacilli}} on a blue background: {{c2::Mycobacterium tuberculosis}}.
Identify the non-enveloped dsDNA virus with {{c1::satellite shape & long antenna-like fibers}}: {{c2::Adenovirus}}.
answer: CPE: Granular clumping / bunch of grapes.

question: Identify the mould-phase {{c1::pear-shaped conidia (lollipop appearance)}} at 25°C: {{c2::Blastomyces dermatitidis}}.
Identify the mould-phase {{c1::tuberculate macroconidia}} at 25°C: {{c2::Histoplasma capsulatum}}.
answer: 37°C yeast: Intracellular inside macrophages.

question: Identify the mould-phase {{c1::barrel-shaped arthrospores (rectangular conidia)}} at 25°C: {{c2::Coccidioides immitis}}.
answer: 37°C tissue: Spherule filled with endospores.

question: Identify the mould-phase pear-shaped conidia of the fungus that forms Mickey-Mouse budding yeast at 37°C: {{c1::Paracoccidioides brasiliensis}}.
Identify the {{c1::bottle-brush conidiophore}} appearance at 25°C (with red pigment on SDA): {{c2::Talaromyces marneffei}}.
answer: 37°C yeast: Oval yeast with transverse septum.

question: Identify the largest brick/box-shaped dsDNA virus: {{c1::Poxvirus}} (300 nm).
Identify the 11-segment dsRNA virus shown: {{c1::Rotavirus}} (Reoviridae).
answer: Contrast: Influenza has 8 RNA segments.

question: Identify the completely double-stranded circular DNA virus shown: {{c1::HPV (Human Papillomavirus)}}.
answer: Contrast: HBV is partially ds circular DNA.

question: Identify the retrovirus containing {{c1::2 identical ssRNA copies}} and reverse transcriptase: {{c2::HIV}}.
answer: Structural genes: env, gag, pol.

question: Identify the baseline supine posture before testing {{c1::neck rigidity}} (difficulty in passive neck flexion due to meningeal irritation): {{c2::Bacterial Meningitis}}.
Identify the Blood agar plate showing α-hemolysis around CSF pneumococcal colonies: {{c1::Streptococcus pneumoniae}}.
Identify the free-living amoeba with {{c1::normal pseudopodia and a bilobed nucleus}} causing subacute SAE: {{c2::Sappinia}}.
Identify the ciliated intestinal protozoan trophozoite shown: {{c1::Balantidium coli}}.
Identify WHO hand hygiene Step 2 shown: {{c1::Rub back of each hand with the other palm, fingers interlaced}}.
answer: Step 3: Palm to palm, fingers interlaced.

question: Identify WHO hand hygiene Step 3 shown: {{c1::Rub palm to palm with fingers interlaced}}.
answer: Step 4: Backs of fingers to opposing palms.

question: Identify WHO hand hygiene Step 5 shown: {{c1::Rotational rubbing of each thumb clasped in opposite palm}}.
answer: Step 6: Rotational rubbing of fingertips on opposite palm.

question: Identify WHO hand hygiene Step 6 shown: {{c1::Rub tips of fingers onto opposite palm in a circular motion}}.
answer: 5 Moments: Before/after patient, before/after procedures, after surroundings.

question: In bacterial conjugation: {{c1::F+ × F-}} transfers the F plasmid making the recipient F+; {{c2::Hfr × F-}} transfers chromosomal DNA (high-frequency recombination) while the recipient usually stays {{c3::F-}}.
answer: R-factor transfer: M/C mechanism of multidrug resistance in Enterobacteriaceae.

question: Compare IMViC reactions: {{c1::E. coli}} = {{c2::++--}} (Indole +ve, MR +ve, VP -ve, Citrate -ve); {{c3::Klebsiella}} = {{c4::--++}} (VP +ve, Citrate +ve).

Gram stain reagents in order: (1) Primary = {{c1::Crystal violet}}, (2) Mordant = {{c2::Gram's iodine}}, (3) Decolorizer = {{c3::Acetone / Alcohol}}, (4) Counterstain = {{c4::Safranin / Carbol fuchsin}}.
Modified Ziehl-Neelsen H2SO4 decolorizer concentrations: M. tuberculosis = {{c1::20%}}; M. leprae = {{c2::5%}}; Nocardia = {{c3::1%}}; Cryptosporidium/Cyclospora = {{c4::0.5–1%}}.

Compare fractional sterilization: {{c1::Tyndallization}} (100°C steam × 20 min for 3 consecutive days; for sugar/gelatin media) vs {{c2::Inspissation}} (80–85°C × 30 min for 3 days; for {{c3::LJ & Loeffler's serum slope}}).

Syphilis serology: Non-treponemal screening & treatment-monitoring tests = {{c1::VDRL / RPR}} (becomes negative after Rx); Specific confirmatory treponemal tests = {{c2::TPHA / FTA-ABS}} (remain lifelong +ve).
answer: Biological false-positive VDRL: SLE, pregnancy, leprosy, malaria.

question: Match Chlamydia trachomatis serotypes: {{c1::A, B, Ba, C}} = Trachoma (blindness); {{c2::D–K}} = Non-gonococcal urethritis / inclusion conjunctivitis; {{c3::L1, L2, L3}} = {{c4::LGV (Lymphogranuloma venereum)}}.

Match E. coli diarrheal pathotypes: {{c1::ETEC}} (LT/ST toxins, traveller's watery diarrhoea), {{c2::EPEC}} (effacement, infants), {{c3::EIEC}} (dysentery, Sereny +ve), {{c4::EHEC O157:H7}} (Shiga-like toxin, HUS, sorbitol-MacConkey pale), {{c5::EAEC}} (stacked-brick adherence).

Match Shigella species (non-motile, non-lactose fermenting, mannite fermentation): Group A = {{c1::S. dysenteriae}} (M/C severe, Shiga toxin, HUS); Group B = {{c2::S. flexneri}}; Group C = {{c3::S. boydii}}; Group D = {{c4::S. sonnei}} (late lactose fermenter).
Typhoid fever culture timeline (BASU): Week 1 = {{c1::Blood culture}}; Week 2 = {{c2::Antibodies (Widal)}}; Week 3 = {{c3::Stool culture}}; Week 4 = {{c4::Urine culture}}.
answer: Bone marrow culture: Remains positive even after antibiotics.

question: Compare Vibrio cholerae biotypes: {{c1::El Tor}} (causes current 7th pandemic) is {{c2::Polymyxin B (50U) resistant}}, VP +ve, Chick RBC agglutination +ve; {{c3::Classical}} is Polymyxin B sensitive, VP -ve.
In nutrient broth with oil/ghee, Yersinia pestis shows {{c1::stalactite growth}} and on Wayson's stain shows {{c2::safety-pin (bipolar) appearance}}.
Proteus species show {{c1::swarming}} on blood/nutrient agar, {{c2::Dienes phenomenon}} (line of demarcation between different strains), and {{c3::Urease +ve}} (alkaline urine → staghorn calculi).
answer: Also: Basis of Weil-Felix heterophile antigens (OX2, OX19, OXK).

question: Clostridium tetani shows {{c1::terminal spherical spores}} giving a {{c2::drumstick / tennis-racket appearance}} on Gram stain.
Diagnosis of C. difficile pseudomembranous colitis: Screen with {{c1::GDH (Glutamate dehydrogenase) antigen}} + confirm with {{c2::Toxin A/B ELISA or NAAT/PCR}}.

Match Staphylococcus aureus toxins: {{c1::Exfoliatin (ET-A/B)}} → Scalded skin syndrome (SSSS); {{c2::TSST-1}} → Toxic shock syndrome; {{c3::Enterotoxin}} → Food poisoning (<6 hrs); {{c4::Panton-Valentine Leukocidin (PVL)}} → Necrotizing pneumonia / MRSA.
answer: Protein A: Binds Fc region of IgG (coagglutination).

question: Compare Streptolysins of S. pyogenes: {{c1::Streptolysin O}} is oxygen-labile and {{c2::antigenic (ASO titre)}} (used to diagnose ARF); {{c3::Streptolysin S}} is oxygen-stable and non-antigenic.
Enterococcus (Group D Strep) grows in {{c1::6.5% NaCl}}, is {{c2::Bile-esculin positive}} (blackening), and {{c3::PYR positive}}.
On Potassium tellurite blood agar, C. diphtheriae biotypes: {{c1::Gravis}} (daisy-head colonies), {{c2::Intermedius}} (frog's egg colonies), {{c3::Mitis}} (poached-egg colonies).
Human Mycobacterium tuberculosis is classically {{c1::Niacin positive}}, {{c2::Nitrate reduction positive}}, and {{c3::Catalase-negative at 68°C}} (lost in INH-resistant strains).

Runyon classification of Non-Tuberculous Mycobacteria: Group I Photochromogens ({{c1::M. marinum, M. kansasii}}), Group II Scotochromogens ({{c2::M. scrofulaceum}}), Group III Non-photochromogens ({{c3::MAC}}), Group IV Rapid growers ({{c4::M. fortuitum, M. chelonae, M. abscessus}}).
Mycobacterium leprae cannot be grown in vitro; it is grown in {{c1::mouse footpad}} or {{c2::nine-banded armadillo}} and shows {{c3::cigar-bundle / globi}} appearance inside Virchow's lepra cells.
answer: Lepromin test: Prognostic (NOT diagnostic); positive in tuberculoid leprosy.

question: Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes Eaton-agent atypical pneumonia, shows {{c1::fried-egg colonies}} on PPLO agar, and triggers {{c2::Cold agglutinins (IgM against I antigen)}}.
Legionella pneumophila (Pontiac fever & Legionnaires' disease) stains poorly on Gram stain (needs {{c1::Dieterle silver stain}}) and grows on {{c2::BCYE (Buffered Charcoal Yeast Extract) agar}}.

Match Rickettsial diseases: {{c1::Epidemic typhus}} (R. prowazekii, Louse, Brill-Zinsser); {{c2::Endemic typhus}} (R. typhi, Flea); {{c3::Scrub typhus}} (Orientia tsutsugamushi, Mite/chigger, eschar); {{c4::RMSF}} (R. rickettsii, Hard tick).

Coxiella burnetii (Q fever) is transmitted primarily by {{c1::inhalation of aerosols from cattle/sheep placenta}} (or soft tick), causes {{c2::culture-negative endocarditis}}, and shows {{c3::NO rash}}.
Bartonella henselae causes {{c1::Cat-scratch disease}} (regional lymphadenitis) and {{c2::Bacillary angiomatosis}} (vascular lesions in HIV mimicking Kaposi's sarcoma).
Borrelia burgdorferi (transmitted by {{c1::Ixodes hard tick}}) causes Lyme disease with {{c2::Erythema migrans (bull's-eye / target rash)}}, Bell's palsy, and AV block.

Severe Leptospirosis ({{c1::Weil's disease}}) presents with hepatorenal failure (jaundice + AKI), calf tenderness, and conjunctival suffusion; diagnosed by {{c2::MAT (Microscopic Agglutination Test)}}.
HBV markers: {{c1::HBsAg +ve > 6 months}} = Chronic HBV; {{c2::Anti-HBs +ve only}} = Vaccinated; {{c3::Anti-HBs + IgG Anti-HBc +ve}} = Resolved natural infection.
HIV binds to {{c1::CD4 receptor}} via {{c2::gp120}} and requires co-receptors {{c3::CCR5}} (macrophage-tropic, early) or {{c4::CXCR4}} (T-cell tropic, late); {{c5::gp41}} mediates membrane fusion.
answer: CCR5 blocker: Maraviroc; gp41 fusion inhibitor: Enfuvirtide.

question: Rabies virus (bullet-shaped Rhabdovirus) produces intracytoplasmic eosinophilic {{c1::Negri bodies}} most commonly in the {{c2::Hippocampus (Ammon's horn)}} and {{c3::Purkinje cells of cerebellum}}.
answer: Antemortem Dx: Nape of neck skin biopsy DFA & Saliva PCR.

question: Compare Influenza variations: {{c1::Antigenic shift}} (major sudden change via genetic reassortment → {{c2::Pandemics}}, Influenza A only) vs {{c3::Antigenic drift}} (minor gradual point mutations → {{c4::Epidemics}}, Influenza A & B).
Cytomegalovirus (HHV-5) produces large intranuclear basophilic {{c1::Owl-eye inclusion bodies}} and is the M/C cause of {{c2::congenital viral infection}} (periventricular calcifications).
Congenital Rubella Syndrome (M/C in 1st trimester) classic triad: {{c1::Cataract (salt-and-pepper retinopathy), Sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL), and Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA)}}.
Zika virus (Flavivirus, transmitted by Aedes mosquito & sexual route) causes congenital {{c1::microcephaly with subcortical calcifications}} and Guillain-Barré syndrome.

Parvovirus B19 (smallest ssDNA virus) binds to {{c1::P antigen (globoside)}} on erythroid precursors → causes {{c2::Erythema infectiosum (slapped cheek)}} in children and {{c3::aplastic crisis}} in sickle cell anemia.

In Malaria, infective form to humans = {{c1::Sporozoites}}; dormant liver stage causing relapse in P. vivax & P. ovale = {{c2::Hypnozoites}} (killed by {{c3::Primaquine}}); infective form to mosquito = {{c4::Gametocytes}}.
answer: P. falciparum & P. malariae: NO hypnozoites (no relapse).

question: Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) screening tests: {{c1::Aldehyde test of Napier}} (hypergammaglobulinemia jellification) and {{c2::rK39 immunochromatographic strip test}} (rapid & specific).
answer: Gold standard: Splenic aspirate > Bone marrow aspirate showing LD bodies.

question: Amoebic liver abscess (Entamoeba histolytica) most commonly affects the {{c1::posterosuperior right lobe}} and yields sterile {{c2::anchovy-sauce pus}}.
Human cysticercosis / Neurocysticercosis is acquired by ingesting {{c1::eggs of Taenia solium}} (NOT undercooked pork, which causes intestinal taeniasis); CT shows {{c2::starry-sky / scolex cysts}}.
answer: Rx: Albendazole + Corticosteroids (to prevent cerebral edema).

question: Hydatid cyst (Echinococcus granulosus): Definitive host = {{c1::Dog}}; Accidental dead-end host = {{c2::Man}}; Imaging shows {{c3::Water-lily sign}} (detached endocyst) / Cartwheel appearance.
answer: Never aspirate blindly without albendazole cover (anaphylactic shock risk).

question: Loeffler's syndrome (transient pulmonary infiltrates + peripheral eosinophilia) occurs during lung migration of {{c1::Ascaris, Hookworm, and Strongyloides}} larvae.
answer: M/c intestinal obstruction in children: Ascaris lumbricoides.

question: Hookworm (Ancylostoma duodenale / Necator americanus) infects humans via {{c1::filariform (L3) larva penetrating skin}} and causes {{c2::microcytic hypochromic (iron deficiency) anemia}}.
answer: Stool microscopy: Non-bile stained egg with segmented blastomeres.

question: Enterobius vermicularis (Pinworm) lays {{c1::planoconvex (D-shaped)}} eggs on perianal skin at night; diagnosed by {{c2::NIH swab / cellophane tape test}} (NOT routine stool exam).
answer: Rx: Albendazole / Mebendazole (treat whole family).

question: Aspergillus clinical spectrum: {{c1::ABPA}} (asthma + central bronchiectasis + ↑IgE, Type 1 & 3 HSR), {{c2::Aspergilloma}} (fungus ball in old TB cavity with {{c3::Monod's air-crescent sign}}), and {{c4::Invasive aspergillosis}} in neutropenia.

Rhinocerebral Mucormycosis classically affects patients with {{c1::Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA), iron overload (deferoxamine), or post-COVID steroids}}, causing necrotic {{c2::black eschar}} on palate/turbinates.
answer: Hyphae: Broad aseptate ribbon-like with 90° branching.

question: In HIV patients with meningitis, {{c1::Cryptococcus neoformans}} shows a clear halo on {{c2::India ink / Nigrosin}} stain, capsular Ag by {{c3::Latex agglutination}}, and brown colonies on {{c4::Bird seed agar}}.
answer: Rx: Liposomal Amp-B + Flucytosine → Fluconazole consolidation.

question: Candida albicans & C. dubliniensis form germ tubes in serum within 2 hours at 37°C — known as the {{c1::Reynolds-Braude phenomenon}}.
answer: Oral thrush: Pseudomembranous white plaque that scrapes off easily leaving erythematous base.

question: Cytokine polarization: {{c1::IL-12}} drives naive CD4 T-cells to {{c2::Th1 (IFN-γ → macrophage activation / CMI)}}; {{c3::IL-4}} drives {{c4::Th2 (IL-4, IL-5 → B-cell Ab & eosinophils / Humoral)}}.

Compare MHC classes: {{c1::MHC Class I}} (all nucleated cells + platelets; binds {{c2::CD8}}; presents endogenous/viral peptides); {{c3::MHC Class II}} (APCs: dendritic, macrophage, B-cell; binds {{c4::CD4}}; presents exogenous peptides).

Positive acute phase reactants (↑ in inflammation): {{c1::CRP, Procalcitonin, Ferritin, Fibrinogen, Hepcidin, Ceruloplasmin}}. Negative acute phase reactants (↓): {{c2::Albumin, Transferrin, Prealbumin}}.
answer: IL-6 is the primary cytokine driving hepatic acute phase protein synthesis.

question: Hyperacute graft rejection (minutes–hours) is due to {{c1::pre-formed recipient antibodies (Type 2 HSR)}} causing fibrinoid necrosis. GVHD occurs when {{c2::donor T-cells in bone marrow/thymus graft}} attack host skin, liver, and gut.

In Robertson Cooked Meat (RCM) broth: {{c1::Saccharolytic}} anaerobes (C. perfringens) turn meat {{c2::pink}}, whereas {{c3::Proteolytic}} anaerobes (C. tetani, C. botulinum) turn meat {{c4::black with foul odor}}.
answer: Advantage: Glutathione & unsaturated fatty acids maintain anaerobiosis.

question: High-yield selective media: C. diphtheriae = {{c1::Potassium tellurite BA}}; Neisseria = {{c2::Thayer-Martin}}; Vibrio = {{c3::TCBS}}; M. tb = {{c4::LJ medium}}; Bordetella = {{c5::Bordet-Gengou}}; Salmonella = {{c6::Wilson-Blair}}.
